gen-fs-quilon-gf-golos-text: Tall, confident, editorial: Quilon swells and thins with a slow rhythm up top. Golos Text takes over below in strokes of one width, with a tall lowercase that fills the line and an s held wide apart.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Quilon brings a commanding editorial look, its strokes swelling and thinning with real modulation, while Hedvig Letters Sans stays nearly flat beneath it. Text runs along smoothly, its c leaving a generous gap.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-heebo: Quilon is made for headings, its strokes shifting gently from thick to thin with large open shapes in a, e and s. Heebo does the opposite job: a tall central band of text and curves that stop short, built for steady paragraphs.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-guntur: Large open counters in a, e and s give Quilon its commanding editorial presence, with only a medium-low contrast between thick and thin parts. Hind Guntur is a steady sans, so give the heading more size.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-madurai: Quilon opens with a soft, steady variation, like a lightly tilted nib, and a commanding editorial voice. Hind Madurai follows in uniform strokes, bent like tubing, with wide s curves and lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru sets lowercase tops close to the ascender height, with no calligraphic thinning and each a left slightly ajar. Hind Mysuru under Quilon's tempered, spring-wire contrast makes long paragraphs feel direct, with diagonals as sturdy as the uprights.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-siliguri: A slow ebb and flow of stroke weight defines Quilon, giving its large open a, e and s an editorial pull. And Hind Siliguri hums along beneath it in flat gray lines, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-vadodara: Quilon's mild, pen-like weight variation gives it an editorial voice. Hind Vadodara follows with the steady line of a drafting pen, its tall-bowled e and a opening wide, so the heading carries the personality and the text stays clean.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-huninn: Huninn is monoline, with lowercase rising close to cap height. Quilon above it swells and thins with a gentle ebb and flow, so paragraphs below that heading read as modern and steady, with crossbars as fat as their stems.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-inter-tight: Slow, brush-soft thickening and thinning gives Quilon a commanding editorial look. And Inter Tight runs beneath it in strokes from one fixed nib, with short ascenders and curve tails held well back.
